scale: directive 1-5: 5 = the packet stated method, order, what to read, what done means and how it is checked, and the model needed nothing else; 3 = it guessed one or two rules or drew refusals; 1 = it read ShipLoop's own source to learn the rules and still misread one that later failed. Packet concise/accurate/effective findings are reused from docs/experiments/packet-review-2026-10-17/A-preparation.json and B-build-1.json (ids A*/B*), not redone.

steps.purpose: Review the test strategy, fix what is warranted, and end on an unchanged pass.
steps.directive_evidence: The review focus drove real finds ('a title-only test', 'no primary-documentation source'). Two reasoning failures trace to the loop rules. The trivial-pass exit invited a deliberate skip: 'I decided not to add the exact-list-equality note... This keeps pass 2 trivial and avoids resetting the required-trivial review count.' 'Replayable' was judged by reading, not by replay: 'The a6a7-to-a8 promotion is confirmed legal.' It is not: a black pawn stands on a7 and a black rook on a8.
steps.response: Partly served: real fixes committed, plus an impossible click sequence and a skipped warranted fix.
steps.improve: Real: the board has no load-FEN control, so page checks became click sequences; castlingBothSides was white-only, so black e8g8/e8c8 and h1h2 oracles were added; a primary source was cited for per-testMethod limits. Cost 3.6 min, 26 calls, 2 passes (126/62 s). Held: step 24 asserts e8g8, e8c8 and h1h2 and the per-method split. Introduced and missed: 'a2 a4, h7 h6, a4 a5, h6 h5, a5 a6, h5 h4, a6 a7, h4 h3, a7 a8' cannot be played (a6-a7 is blocked by the a7 pawn and a8 is occupied). Its python check tested FEN shape only. The sequence went to test-spec, verify and release-verify, and was handed to the owner (step 38: 'a-file queen, a-file knight ... are not-run'). Rubber stamp: pass 2 knowingly left the count-only C1 weakness, which step-plan Improve had to fix ('C1 could pass on a count of 20'), and did not see that the TAP fences test the stale org copy.
gaps: 'a pass that finds none of them is trivial' lets a reviewer label a pass trivial by not acting on what it found. Add 'a pass that sees a warranted fix and leaves it is not trivial: make it or record why not under Found'. Source: shiploop_navigator.py improve_handoff_text (the 'a pass that finds none of them is trivial' sentence) and improve/references/shiploop-route.md review cycle.

The replay focus accepts named inputs. Require mechanical replay for move or click sequences (a script or the product's own rules) with its output in checks.md. Source: shiploop_prompts.py _REVIEW_FOCUS_ITEMS[0].

steps.purpose: Plan the ordered work items, load-bearing assumptions and structure decisions.

LWC metadata files make the test stage mandatory', which folded the engine and board into one item. The summary says 'Tab visibility, if it fails, is recorded at release-verify', and release-verify was blocked on 'Page does not exist' until a permission set the request forbids.

steps.purpose: Review the plan result, fix what is warranted, and end on an unchanged pass.

steps.purpose: Cut W1 into ordered behaviour-level steps with criteria, test commands, a check command, expectations and paths.
steps.directive_evidence: 16 calls into ShipLoop source (shiploop_test_counts.py x3, shiploop_test_loop.py x3, shiploop_expectations.py x3, shiploop_navigator.py x2, item_scope, mutation, scripts grep x3): 'Checking test file detection around lines 2270-2320 to avoid misclassifying the engine as tests.' It misread the check row as a per-criterion inspection: 'This replaces check_na because the packet allows a command check for docs or coverage terms.' It also misread when the check runs: 'It runs after implementation so all files are present.' It overrode the split rule because no step can be proven before the test stage: 'Splitting the engine into multiple steps would leave an incomplete class that cannot compile or be verified until the end.'
steps.response: Did not serve: the gate accepted a plan whose only check row (C12, board grep) fails on S1 and S2, so step 16 had to revise. Criteria and expectations were otherwise sound.
steps.step_by_step: S1 engine (C1-C9, 3 paths), S2 controller (C10-C11), S3 board/tab/app (C12), in order with deps. No step could be proven at its own implement: focused Apex tests are written at the test stage after S3, and the only check row was the S3-only grep, which implement ran from S1. Review was the Improve below. The plan's step granularity existed on paper only, and was collapsed into one step at step 17.
gaps: Duty 3's 'A docs or coverage criterion gets a command check' overloads 'check', which duty 5 uses for the lint/type/build suite. Say 'an inspection command, placed on the step that creates the file (not in suite: check)'. Source: shiploop_prompts.py DUTIES['step-plan'] item 3.

When check rows run was missing; the integration branch added 'The test and verify stages run these; implement runs only each step's own check' to item 5 and the review-focus clause 'a check that needs a later step's work' (B1-1, B2-1). Still missing: a gate refusal for a check row whose criteria belong only to a later step (B1-3). Source: shiploop_navigator.py step-plan result validator; shiploop_stage_spec.py step-plan checked-by.

The split rule ('Split a step with two separately confirmable behaviours') conflicts with 'Tests are not a step', since a step has no proof until the test stage. State the per-step proof: each step names the check or Proof command it can pass alone. The Battleship branch's per-step Proof does this. Source: shiploop_prompts.py DUTIES['step-plan'] item 4.

The scorer facts the model dug out of source (TAP pass line, stderr is captured, the 30-min stage and 10-min command budget, the test-file pattern used to classify paths) are not in the packet. Give one line each beside item 5. Source: shiploop_prompts.py DUTIES['step-plan'] item 5; values from shiploop_test_loop.py and shiploop_item_scope.py.

steps.purpose: Review the step plan, fix what is warranted, and end on an unchanged pass.

steps.improve: Real: C4/C6/C7 lacked the FENs to assert; C11 cited foolsMate as AuraHandledException proof; C1 'could pass on a count of 20'; C5/C8/C10 lacked their FENs and move cycle; the full TAP suite was missing from test_commands. All fixed. Held: step 24 asserts the exact start list a2a3..h2h4, a repeated list, and sizes 48/14/6/44. Cost 5.25 min, 48 calls, 3 passes (183/70/37 s). Missed, with consequence: the C12 row blocked S1 at step 16 (exit 2), forcing a revise, a re-plan to one step (17-20) and a 17.2-min single implement with a compaction. gaps: (Fixed in the integration branch) _REVIEW_FOCUS_STEPS now names 'a check that needs a later step's work or passes by skipping a missing artifact'. Source: shiploop_prompts.py _REVIEW_FOCUS_STEPS.
The 76 KB 'read this whole file' handoff copies producer quotes (B2-2; since replaced by outlines).

run_level.step_by_step: No, by construction before any code. Plan folded engine and board into one item. Step-plan cut S1 engine (C1-C9), S2 controller (C10-C11) and S3 board (C12), but no step had a proof it could pass alone: Apex tests are written only after the last step, and the single check row was the S3-only board grep, which the model believed 'runs after implementation'. Its Improve saw S1 was oversize ('Splitting would delay validation') and made the grep stricter. Both choices led to step 16's revise and the collapse to one step.
run_level.improve: 4 reviews, 11 passes, about 19.4 min (5.24/3.6/5.34/5.25), 145 calls. Real finds that held through the step-24 org tests: six-field FENs and the 6/44 oracles (spec); black castling oracles, the per-testMethod source and click-only board checks (test-strategy); deploy-then-TAP so mutants reach the org (plan); exact-list, FEN and move-cycle oracles for C1/C4-C8/C10 (step-plan). Rubber stamps: test-strategy pass 2 approved an impossible a-file promotion line ('The a6a7-to-a8 promotion is confirmed legal'), which reached the owner unrun at release-verify, and skipped a fix to stay trivial. Plan pass 3 approved an assumption list missing the tab visibility that blocked release-verify. Step-plan pass 3 approved the S1-failing C12 row. Every review checked the content of its result; none checked how ShipLoop would run it (step order, scorer, consumer access).
run_level.directive: Mean 2.9 of 5. Where the stage method was in the packet, the model read nothing else: research 5 (0 guide reads), spec 4, prepare 4, Improve spec 4. Where a rule lived only in ShipLoop's code, the model read the code: step-plan 1 (16 source calls), Improve step-plan 2 (6), discovery 2 (2 source, 14 guide), test-strategy 3 (platform card found by its own grep, test_counts read), Improve plan 2 (navigator.py read for --final-result). Total: 26 calls into skills/shiploop/scripts across 6 of 12 steps, 2 refusals at intake, 1 at Improve plan. The rules it had to dig for: environment.md headings, the reporter/ID-word rule, when check rows run, the scorer's stderr/budget, the --final-result/--notes return, and the assumption consumer form.

best: Research duty 2 'A recalled fact is not evidence' plus duty 4's safe probe: 'I will fetch exact perft counts... rather than recall them' and 'The heap limit is 10 MB, not 6 MB' (3 web searches, 1 anonymous-Apex run, 0 guide reads).

Review focus 'an expected result or check that a weaker stand-in would pass': step-plan Improve found 'C1 could pass on a count of 20' and C11's wrong exception proof; step 24 then asserted the exact start list.

Review focus 'a claim about what the runtime... can do... with no primary-documentation source': test-strategy Improve web-searched and cited the per-testMethod limit that the three-class perf split depends on.
Test-strategy duty 11 'probe it now by doing the case's first step... probe a stand-in': headless Chrome read a RUN/scratch page title before the product existed.
Callback line 'run it exactly as printed... no pipe, redirect': every producer complete call in 01-12 was literal; the only chain was an improve-pass && done at Improve plan.

It runs after implementation'. The result was 16 source reads, then step 16's revise and the collapse from 3 steps to 1.
